import HartshorneLib.Chapter4P1Overlap

/-!
# Laurent coefficient bookkeeping for the two charts of `P1`

The overlap of the standard affine charts is a Laurent polynomial ring.  This
file packages the coefficient at `T⁻¹` as a linear functional and records the
formal cancellation with the opposite boundary contribution.  These are
algebraic overlap statements only; identifying them with intrinsic geometric
residues is a later producer obligation.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open LaurentPolynomial

namespace Hartshorne

noncomputable section

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]

/-- The coefficient functional at the Laurent exponent `n`. -/
noncomputable def laurentCoefficient (n : ℤ) : LaurentPolynomial k →ₗ[k] k :=
  Finsupp.lapply n

@[simp]
theorem laurentCoefficient_apply (n : ℤ) (f : LaurentPolynomial k) :
    laurentCoefficient n f = f n := by
  change (Finsupp.lapply n) f = _
  rw [Finsupp.lapply_apply]

theorem laurentCoefficient_single (n m : ℤ) (a : k) :
    laurentCoefficient n (AddMonoidAlgebra.single m a) =
      if m = n then a else 0 := by
  change (Finsupp.lapply n) (AddMonoidAlgebra.single m a) = _
  rw [Finsupp.lapply_apply]
  rw [Finsupp.single_apply]

theorem laurentCoefficient_monomial (n m : ℤ) (a : k) :
    laurentCoefficient n (LaurentPolynomial.C a * LaurentPolynomial.T m) =
      if m = n then a else 0 := by
  rw [← LaurentPolynomial.single_eq_C_mul_T a m]
  exact laurentCoefficient_single n m a

/-- The finite-chart residue coefficient of a Laurent overlap expression. -/
noncomputable def laurentResidueAtZero : LaurentPolynomial k →ₗ[k] k :=
  laurentCoefficient (-1)

/-- The opposite boundary contribution in the two-chart Laurent bookkeeping. -/
noncomputable def laurentResidueAtInfinity : LaurentPolynomial k →ₗ[k] k :=
  -laurentResidueAtZero

@[simp]
theorem laurentResidueAtZero_apply (f : LaurentPolynomial k) :
    laurentResidueAtZero f = f (-1) := by
  rw [laurentResidueAtZero, laurentCoefficient_apply]

@[simp]
theorem laurentResidueAtInfinity_apply (f : LaurentPolynomial k) :
    laurentResidueAtInfinity f = -f (-1) := by
  change -(laurentResidueAtZero f) = _
  rw [laurentResidueAtZero_apply]

theorem laurentResidueAtZero_add_atInfinity (f : LaurentPolynomial k) :
    laurentResidueAtZero f + laurentResidueAtInfinity f = 0 := by
  change laurentResidueAtZero f + -(laurentResidueAtZero f) = 0
  exact add_neg_cancel _

theorem laurentResidueAtZero_monomial (a : k) (n : ℤ) :
    laurentResidueAtZero (LaurentPolynomial.C a * LaurentPolynomial.T n) =
      if n = -1 then a else 0 := by
  exact laurentCoefficient_monomial (-1) n a

/-! ### Polynomial and inverse-chart contributions -/

/-- A polynomial in the affine coordinate has no `T⁻¹` coefficient. -/
theorem laurentResidueAtZero_toLaurent (p : Polynomial k) :
    laurentResidueAtZero (Polynomial.toLaurent p) = 0 := by
  induction p using Polynomial.induction_on' with
  | add p q =>
      rw [map_add (Polynomial.toLaurent) p q]
      rw [(laurentResidueAtZero (k := k)).map_add,
        ‹laurentResidueAtZero (Polynomial.toLaurent p) = 0›,
        ‹laurentResidueAtZero (Polynomial.toLaurent q) = 0›, add_zero]
  | monomial n a =>
      rw [show Polynomial.monomial n a = Polynomial.C a * Polynomial.X ^ n by
        rw [Polynomial.C_mul_X_pow_eq_monomial]]
      rw [Polynomial.toLaurent_C_mul_X_pow]
      rw [laurentResidueAtZero, laurentCoefficient_monomial]
      simp

/-- The inverse-chart polynomial contributes its degree-one coefficient to the
`T⁻¹` coefficient on the overlap. -/
theorem laurentResidueAtZero_aeval_inv (q : Polynomial k) :
    laurentResidueAtZero
        (Polynomial.aeval (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) : LaurentPolynomial k) q) =
      q.coeff 1 := by
  induction q using Polynomial.induction_on' with
  | add p q =>
      rw [map_add (Polynomial.aeval (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) : LaurentPolynomial k)) p q]
      rw [(laurentResidueAtZero (k := k)).map_add, ‹laurentResidueAtZero (Polynomial.aeval
          (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) : LaurentPolynomial k) p) = p.coeff 1›,
        ‹laurentResidueAtZero (Polynomial.aeval
          (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) : LaurentPolynomial k) q) = q.coeff 1›,
        Polynomial.coeff_add]
  | monomial n a =>
      rw [Polynomial.aeval_monomial, ← LaurentPolynomial.C_eq_algebraMap]
      rw [LaurentPolynomial.T_pow]
      rw [laurentResidueAtZero, laurentCoefficient_monomial]
      simp [Polynomial.coeff_monomial]

/-- On a Laurent decomposition, the boundary coefficient is exactly the
degree-one coefficient of the inverse-chart polynomial. -/
theorem laurentResidueAtZero_of_toLaurent_add_aeval
    (p q : Polynomial k) :
    laurentResidueAtZero
        (Polynomial.toLaurent p +
          Polynomial.aeval (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) : LaurentPolynomial k) q) =
      q.coeff 1 := by
  rw [(laurentResidueAtZero (k := k)).map_add, laurentResidueAtZero_toLaurent,
    laurentResidueAtZero_aeval_inv, zero_add]

/-! ### Boundary cancellation on the standard two-chart cover -/

/-- The opposite chart boundary reads the negative of the degree-one coefficient
of its inverse-coordinate polynomial. -/
theorem laurentResidueAtInfinity_of_toLaurent_add_aeval
    (p q : Polynomial k) :
    laurentResidueAtInfinity
        (Polynomial.toLaurent p +
          Polynomial.aeval (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) : LaurentPolynomial k) q) =
      -q.coeff 1 := by
  change -laurentResidueAtZero
      (Polynomial.toLaurent p +
        Polynomial.aeval (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) : LaurentPolynomial k) q) = _
  rw [laurentResidueAtZero_of_toLaurent_add_aeval]

/-- The two chart-boundary contributions cancel for every Laurent overlap
decomposition.  This is the algebraic P1 residue theorem prior to identifying
the coefficient functionals with intrinsic geometric residues. -/
theorem laurentBoundaryResidue_sum_eq_zero
    (p q : Polynomial k) :
    laurentResidueAtZero
        (Polynomial.toLaurent p +
          Polynomial.aeval (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) : LaurentPolynomial k) q) +
      laurentResidueAtInfinity
        (Polynomial.toLaurent p +
          Polynomial.aeval (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) : LaurentPolynomial k) q) = 0 := by
  rw [laurentResidueAtZero_of_toLaurent_add_aeval,
    laurentResidueAtInfinity_of_toLaurent_add_aeval]
  exact add_neg_cancel _

/-- Every Laurent polynomial admits a two-chart decomposition whose opposite
boundary contribution is the negative degree-one inverse-chart coefficient. -/
theorem exists_laurentBoundaryResidue_decomposition
    (f : LaurentPolynomial k) :
    ∃ p q : Polynomial k,
      f = Polynomial.toLaurent p +
        Polynomial.aeval (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) : LaurentPolynomial k) q ∧
      laurentResidueAtInfinity f = -q.coeff 1 := by
  obtain ⟨p, q, h⟩ := LaurentPolynomial.exists_toLaurent_add_aeval f
  refine ⟨p, q, h, ?_⟩
  rw [h, laurentResidueAtInfinity_of_toLaurent_add_aeval]

end
end Hartshorne
